newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed in thin trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a very quiet session mixed, with March marks, Swiss and sterling all higher.
Traders said trading pits were noticeably thin before the upcoming Christmas holiday week, and most action was tied to position-squaring.
"It was a lot of locals, with almost no paper coming through," one IMM trader said.
"We really just traded off the stock market," he said. "The Dow would tick down a few ticks and we'd tick up a few down here."
Swiss, sterling and marks all posted inside days on daily bar charts, a noncommital technical signal, one trader said.
Traders said profit-taking from declines on Thursday in Swiss and marks helped buoy those markets initially, but both contracts were unable to follow through much to the upside.

March yen slipped to a 2-1/2-week low, hampered by worries of selling above the market. Yen slipped as low as $0.008848 early in the session and hovered near there into the close. Activity all but dried up after the initial drop, traders said.

At settlement, March yen were off $0.000025 to $0.008854, marks were up $0.0015 to $0.6474, Swiss francs rose $0.0013 to $0.7551, sterling rose $0.0048 to $1.6664, Canadian dollars were off $0.0006 at $0.7352, Australian dollars rose $0.0003 to $0.7940, and Mexican pesos rose $0.000225 to $0.121450.
